title: Wrong Items Kept by the Customer: Delivery Claims Keep Charge and Customer Authorization
content:
**Rule.** On a Delivery Claims Wrong Item Claim the wrong item is sent back with a prepaid label within the claim type's item return window, in calendar days of approval, or the customer keeps it and is charged the wrong-item keep charge, recorded as a wrong item not returned.

Keeping the wrong item and paying for it is the customer's own decision: the customer authorizes the keep charge personally, for the order line the wrong item came in place of, and the charge goes to the original card. A wrong-item keep charge is booked while the claim is in status approved or resolved.

The keep charge for a wrong item is fixed only after any delivery-charge refund owed on its claim stands on the claim. A wrong-item keep charge is taken only after the compensation owed on each of the customer's other approved claims has been booked.

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| Who decides to keep the wrong item | the customer |
| Who authorizes the charge | the customer personally |
| What the charge is for | the order line the wrong item came in place of |
| Where the charge goes | the original card |
| Claim status in which the charge is booked | approved or resolved |

## Customer action: `authorize_wrong_item_keep_charge_d92bb3d2`

**Situation of use and capability.** The customer authorizes the charge to their original card for a wrong item they received and choose to keep instead of sending it back. It serves a customer whose parcel brought an item other than the one ordered, whose Wrong Item Claim has been approved, and who would rather keep the item received than return it with the prepaid label. One call records a single charge on the claim for the order line the wrong item came in place of: the number of units kept and the amount the customer agrees to be charged, dated today, taken from the card the order was paid with. The claim is not otherwise changed. The recorded charge shows on the claim as value recovered for a wrong item kept.

**How it is invoked.** This is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks it for the customer with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `claim_id` | the claim number of the customer's Wrong Item Claim, as the representative reads it to the customer from the claim record | identifier |
| `booked_line_id` | the order line reference number (the identifier of the booked order line) the wrong item came in place of, as the representative reads it from the claim record | identifier |
| `quantity` | how many units the customer keeps | a whole number, at least 1 |
| `amount_usd` | the amount the customer authorizes to be charged, in USD, as the representative states it; recorded on the claim as value recovered | a positive amount rounded to 2 decimal places (to the nearest cent, on the final figure) |

**Return.** A text rendering of a dictionary with `charge_id` (the reference of the recorded charge), `claim_id` (the claim number), `booked_line_id` (the order line concerned), `quantity` (units kept), `amount_charged_usd` (the amount taken from the card, USD with 2 decimal places) and `charged_on` (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD). Receiving this receipt means the charge has been authorized and recorded.
